text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card and the tone is cautious. But the narrative has an unsupported claim about duplicates, an overstatement in the headline, and cited claims that do not fit their sentences. An investigator would need to check some of it again.","problems":["The claim that 'about two-thirds of returned notes were flagged as duplicates' does not appear on the evidence card, and the note-check list in the summary shows only problems, late, unsigned and data. Nothing visible supports it. The headline's 'high share of duplicated notes' rests on the same claim.","The headline says 99215 is above expectation 'in every complexity stratum'. The 4-condition band is 0.182 against 0.105, under two times, so 'three to four times in each band' is wrong. The ratios run from about 1.7x to 6x.","The statement that sampled charts 'largely support' the billed level rests on only 16 documented 99215s, and the sample is not shown to be representative.","C0019149 is cited as the single mismatch, but it is a Z09 follow-up billed 99215 with moderate MDM and 38 minutes. This is mild evidence and the summary uses it without caveat.","The summary says the 'supported' examples C0019078 and C0019464 show high MDM on low-complexity patients. That fits the card, but it is used to infer cloning without any evidence of duplicate text for those notes.","The cited low-complexity examples (J06.9, N39.0, Z09) are described as 'single-problem diagnoses', which is an interpretation, and most of those claims have no documentation in the packet.","Leaning 'inconclusive' fits the evidence, but the next steps are generic. They name three claims, and two of them (C0019013, C0019032) have no documentation. The steps do not point to the duplicate-note comparison or the audit trail that the rationale recommends."]}
